If the contractor fails to complete the work, the client can invoke the BG and recover the guaranteed amount from the bank. **Typical PBG value**: 5-10% of contract value (some government projects up to 15%). For a ₹100 crore project at 5% PBG, that's ₹5 crore tied up in the BG. Validity typically covers the construction period + defect liability period (3-12 months post-completion). **The Performance BG Submission Letter** is the formal cover document that transmits the BG instrument from the contractor to the client. It records: BG number, issuing bank, amount, validity period, BG type (conditional / unconditional), and beneficiary details. Without this letter, the BG submission has no audit trail; clients cannot tie the BG to the specific contract. #### Key elements of the submission **Mandatory contents** (Clause-level): 1\. **Contract reference** — contract number, date, work description 2\. **BG details** — bank name, branch, BG instrument number, BG date 3\. **Amount in figures + words** — must match contract requirement exactly 4\. **Validity period** — start date + end date; must cover construction period + DLP 5\. **BG type** — conditional (bank verifies before paying) vs unconditional / on-demand (pays immediately upon client invocation) 6\. **Beneficiary** — exact legal name of client / employer 7\. **Issuing authority** — authorized signatory of the contractor company 8\. **Acknowledgment field** — client receipt acknowledgment **Standard practice**: contractors issue PBG within 28-30 days of contract award (per most Indian contracts). Delay = liquidated damages or contract termination. **Renewal**: when validity nears expiry, contractor must extend or replace. Late renewal = invocation risk for client. #### Common BG-related disputes 1\. **BG amount mismatch** — letter says ₹5 cr but BG instrument says ₹50 lakh (decimal point error). Client rejects; contractor re-issues; delay + cost. 2\. **Wrong beneficiary name** — contractor names parent company instead of specific subsidiary that signed the contract. Client can't invoke; useless. 3\. **Conditional BG when unconditional required** — government contracts typically require unconditional / on-demand BGs. Some contractors submit conditional to retain control; client rejects. 4\. **Validity expiry** — BG expires before project complete + DLP done; if expired, client cannot invoke; effectively no guarantee. 5\. **Inadequate validity** — BG covers only construction period, not DLP. Defects emerging during DLP cannot be recovered against BG. 6\. **Bank revocation** — issuing bank withdraws BG due to contractor's financial issues; client loses guarantee. Verify bank's BG is irrevocable. 7\. **No proper acknowledgment** — letter submitted without client's stamped receipt; later dispute about whether BG was actually submitted on time. #### Cross-references **Companion formats**: \- [Performance BG itself (FMT-TND-014)](https://infralens.in/formats/tendering) — the actual BG instrument (issued by bank) \- [Letter of Award (FMT-TND-014)](https://infralens.in/formats/tendering/FMT-TND-014_Letter_of_Award_LOA) — contract award trigger \- [Deviation Sheet — Commercial (FMT-TND-012)](https://infralens.in/formats/tendering/FMT-TND-012_Deviation_Sheet_Commercial) — for any BG-related deviations \- Insurance certificates — companion financial documents (Performance Insurance is sometimes accepted in lieu of BG) **Standards / contract types**: \- **FIDIC** standard contracts (Red Book, Yellow Book, Silver Book) — international project standard; PBG terms in General Conditions Clause 4.2 \- **NHAI standard EPC contract** — PBG terms specified \- **MoRTH standard contracts** — bridge / highway projects \- **CPWD General Conditions of Contract** — building works \- **State PWD General Conditions** — public works \- **Indian Contract Act 1872** — Section 126 (contracts of guarantee) ### Related Formats — Tendering & Contracts - 📐 [Pre-Qualification (PQ) Application\\ \\ form · FMT-TND-001](https://infralens.in/formats/tendering/pre-qualification-pq-application) - 📐 [Technical Bid Compliance Sheet\\ \\ form · FMT-TND-002](https://infralens.in/formats/tendering/technical-bid-compliance-sheet) - 📐 [Financial Bid — Item Rate\\ \\ form · FMT-TND-003](https://infralens.in/formats/tendering/financial-bid-item-rate) - 📐 [Financial Bid — Percentage Rate\\ \\ form · FMT-TND-004](https://infralens.in/formats/tendering/financial-bid-percentage-rate) - 📐 [BOQ Format (CPWD-style)\\ \\ schedule · FMT-TND-005](https://infralens.in/formats/tendering/boq-format-cpwd-style) - 📐 [BOQ Format (PWD-style)\\ \\ schedule · FMT-TND-006](https://infralens.in/formats/tendering/boq-format-pwd-style)
